status: PRE-REGISTERED — written before the window opens (2026-07-27) and before any outcome is known.
purpose: H2 as originally written compares the forced binary calls against 50%. That baseline is wrong: these propositions do not have 50% base rates. The prior prediction-validation study hit exactly this problem — its control scored 72.2% by following the market, so beating a coin told us nothing. This file fixes the baseline BEFORE resolution so H2 can be scored as lift over base rate rather than lift over chance.

method_tags.reference_class: A documented long-run frequency exists for this class of event (earnings-beat rates, incumbent renomination rates, USGS/NHC climatology, prior editions of the same competition).
method_tags.structural: The proposition's own form fixes the rate — a two-week directional move in a liquid asset is ~0.5 plus drift, a single preseason game is ~0.5.
method_tags.subjective: No external anchor. This is the caster's judgment and should be read as the weakest kind of entry here.

known_weakness: The same agent that made the 60 predictions is estimating these base rates, on the same day. The estimates are frozen in git before the window opens, which makes them non-adjustable but not independent. A genuinely clean version would have a separate party set them. Treat `subjective` rows accordingly.
scoring_rule: For prediction c_i in {YES,NO} with base rate p_i, the null probability that call i is correct is p_i if c_i=YES else (1-p_i). Expected hits under the null is the sum of those. Observed hits are compared to that Poisson-binomial distribution, one-tailed. H2 is supported only if the hexagram-derived calls beat this, not 50%.
